nodes.title: Text (user_prompt)
widgets_values: A raw, high-resolution 35mm documentary portrait of an artisan ceramicist in her sunlit studio loft, shot on a Leica M11 with a 50mm f/1.4 lens. The composition is a natural three-quarters candid portrait bathed in cool morning daylight streaming from a tall steel-framed window on the left, balanced by soft room fill. The woman, in her late 40s, is the primary subject: her face displays authentic, unretouched skin texture with visible pores, delicate fine lines around her eyes, subtle natural asymmetry, and a faint dusting of dry white clay powder across her cheekbone. Her dark hair is pulled back into an informal bun with flyaway silver-grey strands catching the rim light. She wears a faded navy-blue canvas work apron over a charcoal waffle-knit henley with visible fabric weave and small frayed edges. Her hands, resting casually on the edge of a rustic pine workbench, show dry knuckles and fingernails lightly lined with terracotta slip. The workbench in the immediate foreground features genuine clutter: a damp sponge, a wire trimming loop, an open sketchbook with faint pencil cross-hatching, and a half-empty stoneware mug of black coffee with a subtle oily sheen on the liquid surface. The background falls into a creamy, organic depth of field showing stacked wooden drying racks with unglazed pottery and the soft blur of a studio brick wall. The image features natural color grading with earthy ochres, slate blues, and warm skin tones, crisp focus on the iris of her left eye, and no artificial plastic smoothing or HDR haloing.
